subject: What happens during a home consultation
hook: What actually happens when a furniture designer comes round? Here is the visit, step by step.
ig:
What actually happens when a furniture designer comes round? Here is the visit, step by step.

A lot of people put off booking a design consultation because they are not sure what it involves. So here it is, plainly:

→ We start with how you use the room, not with a brochure.
→ We look at what shapes the design: alcoves, ceiling height, sockets, radiators, windows and skirting.
→ Finish samples come out in your own light, because oak-effect and charcoal look different by a north-facing window than they do in a showroom.
→ Rough layouts get talked through with you, so you can say what works before anything is drawn up.
→ Once the direction is agreed, we measure properly and send an itemised quote, with every part of the job listed.

To get the most from it, have your must-haves written down and take a few photos of what you currently store in the room.

Save this for when you book, and use the link in bio to arrange your free, no-obligation consultation.
fb:
If you have never had a bespoke furniture consultation before, it is fair to wonder what you are letting yourself in for.

Here is how ours go. We start by asking how you actually use the room. We look at the bits that shape a design, like alcoves, radiators and where the sockets are. Samples come out so you can see finishes in your own light. Then, once you are happy with the direction, we measure properly and put together an itemised quote so you can see exactly what you are paying for.

It is free, there is no obligation, and you are welcome to ask as many questions as you like. Swipe through for the full walkthrough, and book yours here:
